nodes.summary: Shared type definitions (Chunk, ChunkerConfig) and default configuration constants for the smart-chunker module family.

nodes.name: smart-chunker.ts
nodes.summary: Format-aware chunking dispatcher and barrel facade that routes file content to the right chunker (markdown/JSON/YAML/code/fixed) by extension, applies post-processing, and optionally prefixes chunks with file-path and section-label context headers for embedding.
nodes.languageNotes: Classic TypeScript barrel: re-exports the entire chunker/ submodule surface (types, per-format chunkers, post-processing) alongside its own dispatch logic, so downstream consumers across the codebase only need one import path.

nodes.name: firstContentLine
nodes.summary: Returns the first non-comment, non-blank line of chunk content, used to build a short preview snippet for intent search results.

nodes.name: searchSections
nodes.summary: Scores and ranks smartChunk-produced sections against a tokenized intent query using term-frequency plus a label-match boost, returning the top-N matching sections.

nodes.name: distinctiveTerms
nodes.summary: Computes the most distinctive vocabulary terms across sections using a document-frequency-weighted score, used to surface vocabulary hints when intent search returns weak or no matches.

nodes.name: intentSearch
nodes.summary: Entry point that chunks execute/execute_file output via smartChunk, ranks sections against the caller's intent query, and returns matched sections with vocabulary hints and truncation metadata — only triggered when output exceeds INTENT_SEARCH_THRESHOLD.

nodes.name: renderIntentResult
nodes.summary: Formats an intent search result into a human/agent-readable text report listing matched sections, byte savings, and vocabulary hints.

nodes.name: chunkCode
nodes.summary: Splits source code into chunks at detected declaration boundaries (classes, functions, methods), falling back to fixed-size chunking when no boundaries are found, and folds a small leading preamble (imports/comments) into the first chunk.

nodes.name: findCodeBoundaries
nodes.summary: Scans source lines with regex patterns to locate top-level container declarations (class/interface/enum/etc.) and method-level declarations, tracking brace depth via a container stack to distinguish top-level from nested code.

nodes.name: netBraceDelta
nodes.summary: Computes the net change in brace depth for a line of code after stripping string and comment literals, used to track nesting while scanning for code boundaries.

nodes.name: extractFileImports
nodes.summary: Extracts the leading import/require statement block from a source file's content based on its extension, used to attach file-level import context to code chunks.

nodes.name: chunkJSON
nodes.summary: Chunks a JSON object by its top-level keys, serializing each key's value back into a labeled sub-chunk; falls back to fixed-size chunking for arrays, primitives, or invalid JSON.

nodes.name: chunkYAML
nodes.summary: Chunks YAML content first by multi-document `---` separators, then by top-level keys within each document, merging trivial or comment-only sections.

nodes.name: chunkMarkdown
nodes.summary: Entry point for markdown chunking — dispatches to heading-based chunking when the content contains Markdown headings, otherwise falls back to fixed-size chunking.

nodes.name: chunkMarkdownByHeadings
nodes.summary: Splits markdown content into sections at heading boundaries, building a breadcrumb-style label (e.g. 'Title > Section A') from the heading hierarchy stack for each chunk.

nodes.name: postProcess
nodes.summary: Second pass over chunker output that merges undersized chunks (below minChunkLines) into the previous chunk and splits oversized chunks via splitOversizedChunk, enforcing per-format line/char budgets.

nodes.name: splitOversizedChunk
nodes.summary: Splits a single oversized chunk into smaller sub-chunks at blank-line boundaries where possible, falling back to character-budget splitting via splitLineByChars for individual long lines.

nodes.name: splitLineByChars
nodes.summary: Splits a single very long line into multiple parts at word boundaries where possible, respecting a maximum character budget per part.

nodes.name: chunkFixed
nodes.summary: Fallback chunker that splits content into fixed-size line windows, used by every format-specific chunker when no smarter strategy applies or parsing fails.

nodes.name: smartChunk
nodes.summary: Main chunking dispatcher — selects a format-specific chunker by file extension (markdown/JSON/YAML/code/fixed), runs post-processing, and optionally prefixes each chunk with file-path and section-label context headers for embedding.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: OpenCode plugin entry point that registers massa-ai's search, memory, indexing, compression, and symbol-graph tools as OpenCode tool handlers, and wires session-start, post-tool-use, compaction, shell-env, and generic event hooks to the massa-ai REST API and the ObservationEmitter for lifecycle telemetry.
nodes.languageNotes: Repeats an AbortController + setTimeout fetch-timeout pattern across three HTTP helpers, and returns a single large Plugin object literal (tool handlers + host lifecycle hooks) matching the @opencode-ai/plugin contract.

nodes.name: observation-emitter.ts
nodes.summary: Batches and debounces lifecycle observation events (tool use, prompts, sessions) and POSTs them to massa-ai's hook ingest endpoint, mirroring the Claude-plugin hook scripts by emitting raw host events for server-side classification rather than classifying them itself.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a fully injectable EmitterDeps interface (post/log/enabled/now/setTimer/clearTimer) so the batching and debounce logic is unit-testable without real timers or network calls; makeDefaultDeps wires the real fetch/setTimeout implementation.

nodes.name: session-project-pin.ts
nodes.summary: Memoizes a per-session project id computed via project id > git toplevel basename > directory basename > "default" precedence, plus an agentIdOf helper, so an OpenCode plugin session consistently attributes events to the same project even from subdirectory contexts.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a bounded memo (default 1000 sessions) with oldest-key eviction using Map insertion order as an implicit LRU/FIFO structure.

nodes.name: index.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for MassaAiPlugin covering every registered tool's execute(), the session/tool/compaction/shell-env/event lifecycle hooks, and the internal massaAiFetch/massaAiGet HTTP helpers, using mocked fetch and captured log/toast calls.

nodes.name: observation-emitter.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for ObservationEmitter verifying batching thresholds, debounce-based flush scheduling, dispose semantics, and failure handling using a fake EmitterDeps with controllable timers and a captured post function.

nodes.name: session-project-pin.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for SessionProjectPin's per-session id memoization and eviction behavior alongside computePluginProjectId's fallback precedence.

nodes.name: ensureConfig
nodes.summary: Auto-initializes the massa-ai config file with defaults on first run and prints a one-time setup banner pointing at the config path and provider-switch commands.

nodes.name: massaAiFetch
nodes.summary: Generic POST helper to the massa-ai REST API with an AbortController-based timeout, throwing a descriptive error on non-OK responses.

nodes.name: massaAiGet
nodes.summary: Generic GET helper to the massa-ai REST API with an AbortController-based timeout, mirroring massaAiFetch's error handling.

nodes.name: massaAiGetWithQuery
nodes.summary: Builds a URL query string from a params record, skipping undefined/null values, and delegates to massaAiGet.

nodes.name: MassaAiPlugin
nodes.summary: The OpenCode Plugin factory: registers the search/remember/recall/index/compress/optimized_context/read/index_status/analytics/list_projects/search_definitions/get_references/go_to_definition tools plus session/tool/compaction/shell-env/event/dispose lifecycle hooks, wiring them to the massa-ai REST API, SessionProjectPin, and ObservationEmitter.

nodes.name: buildToolPayload
nodes.summary: Converts an OpenCode tool call (name, args, output, cwd, sessionId) into the snake_case payload shape the server's observation classifier expects.

nodes.name: buildPromptPayload
nodes.summary: Builds a user-prompt observation payload including message/text aliases consumed server-side by classifyUserPrompt.

nodes.name: buildSessionPayload
nodes.summary: Builds a session-start/session-end observation payload from optional cwd, sessionId, model, settings, and env fields.

nodes.name: makeDefaultDeps
nodes.summary: Constructs the default EmitterDeps implementation backed by global fetch/setTimeout/Date.now, used to wire ObservationEmitter against the real runtime.

nodes.name: ObservationEmitter
nodes.summary: Batches lifecycle observation events and flushes them to the massa-ai hook-batch endpoint on a size/time debounce, swallowing network failures so emission never blocks the plugin's primary functions.

nodes.name: computePluginProjectId
nodes.summary: Resolves the plugin's project id using precedence: explicit projectId > git toplevel basename > directory basename > "default".

nodes.name: gitToplevelSafe
nodes.summary: Runs `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` via spawnSync with a 1s timeout, silently degrading to undefined on any failure or non-zero exit.

nodes.name: agentIdOf
nodes.summary: Extracts a host-provided agent id from an arbitrary event object, returning undefined when absent or not a non-empty string.

nodes.name: SessionProjectPin
nodes.summary: Per-session memo of a computed project id with bounded (default 1000-entry) eviction, so subsequent events in the same session reuse the first computed id.

nodes.name: makePluginInput
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a fake OpenCode PluginInput (project, directory, worktree, client with log/toast capture arrays) for exercising MassaAiPlugin in isolation.

nodes.name: mockFetchCapture
nodes.summary: Test helper that stubs globalThis.fetch to capture outgoing requests and optionally return a custom Response via a responder callback.

nodes.name: makeFakeDeps
nodes.summary: Test helper that builds a fake EmitterDeps implementation recording logs, timers, and posted batches for deterministic ObservationEmitter testing.

nodes.name: dashboard-views.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the dashboard.js pure renderers, feeding deterministic fixtures into each observability section (scheduler, hook queue, Synapse sessions, system metrics) and asserting the resulting HTML, including running/empty/error/unavailable states.

nodes.name: web-ui-readonly.test.ts
nodes.summary: Enforces the Web UI's read-only guarantee by statically scanning app.js for every api.request() target and asserting none resolve to a forbidden mutating path, plus verifies write-mode-gated buttons only render when MASSA_AI_WEB_WRITE_MODE is enabled.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a regex-based static extraction of request() call targets plus a 'discrimination sensor' mutation test — it injects a fake mutating call into the source text and asserts the same assertion logic would catch it, guarding against a vacuously-passing test.

nodes.name: web-ui-render.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for app.js's markdownToHtml renderer (headings, bold/italic, inline/fenced code, lists, safe links, HTML-escaping) and the toggleTheme/initTheme dark-mode helpers exercised against fake document and localStorage doubles.

nodes.name: web-ui-views.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for app.js's HTML view renderers (projects, memory browser, search, handoffs, checkpoints), asserting each produces the expected fragments for populated, filtered, empty, and error-response fixtures matching the real REST response shapes.

nodes.name: app.js
nodes.summary: Core client-side module for the read-only massa-ai Web UI: HTML view renderers for projects/memory/search/handoffs/proposals/checkpoints, a hand-rolled markdown-to-HTML fallback, dark-mode theming, a minimal fetch-based API client, and the startApp bootstrap that wires hash-routing and DOM events.
nodes.languageNotes: Dual-mode module: uses ESM `export` for pure helpers (testable via Bun's require() without a DOM) while also attaching everything to `globalThis.MASSA_AI_UI` and self-invoking startApp() when `document` exists, so the same source serves both the browser and the Bun test runner.

nodes.name: dashboard.js
nodes.summary: Read-only dashboard module that fetches scheduler, hook-queue, Synapse-session, and system-metrics data in parallel via Promise.allSettled and renders each into an independent HTML section, degrading a single section to 'unavailable' instead of failing the whole page.

nodes.name: isWriteModeEnabled
nodes.summary: Checks whether write-mode UI controls (edit/delete/approve buttons) should render, gated by the globalThis.MASSA_AI_WEB_WRITE_MODE flag or a persisted localStorage preference, defaulting to false.

nodes.name: escapeHtml
nodes.summary: Escapes &, <, >, and " in a string to their HTML entities to prevent injected markup when interpolating untrusted content into rendered views.

nodes.name: markdownToHtml
nodes.summary: Converts a markdown string to sanitized HTML, preferring the `marked` + `DOMPurify` libraries when available in the browser and falling back to the hand-rolled `_minimalMarkdownToHtml` parser otherwise (e.g. under Bun test).

nodes.name: _minimalMarkdownToHtml
nodes.summary: Hand-rolled markdown-to-HTML fallback parser supporting headings, bold/italic, inline and fenced code, ordered/unordered lists, links, and paragraphs, used when the marked/DOMPurify libraries are unavailable.
nodes.languageNotes: Line-by-line state machine with local flushLists/flushPara/inline helper closures instead of a dependency on a full markdown library, keeping the read-only UI's test environment dependency-free.

nodes.name: renderProjects
nodes.summary: Renders the indexed-projects list view as an HTML list of project IDs with document counts, showing an explicit empty state when no projects are indexed.

nodes.name: renderMemoryBrowser
nodes.summary: Renders the memory browser view: filter controls (type/level/minImportance), a paginated table of memory rows with markdown-rendered content, and write-mode-gated edit/delete action buttons; handles error and empty-result states.

nodes.name: renderSearch
nodes.summary: Renders the semantic search view, showing a prompt when the query is empty, an empty-results message echoing the query, or a list of scored, markdown-rendered result snippets.

nodes.name: renderHandoffs
nodes.summary: Renders the pending cross-agent handoffs view as cards showing target agent, status, and markdown-rendered summary, prompting for a project selection or showing an empty state when appropriate.

nodes.name: renderProposals
nodes.summary: Renders the pending proposals view as cards with type, status, and markdown-rendered description, including write-mode-gated approve/reject action buttons.

nodes.name: renderCheckpoints
nodes.summary: Renders the checkpoints list view as a table of task ID, type, status, and description, extracting rows defensively from the checkpoints response shape and showing an error/empty state when needed.

nodes.name: initTheme
nodes.summary: Applies the persisted dark/light theme from storage to the document's data-theme attribute on startup, defaulting to light when no preference is stored.

nodes.name: toggleTheme
nodes.summary: Flips the current light/dark theme, applies it to the document's data-theme attribute, and persists the new preference to storage.

nodes.name: createApiClient
nodes.summary: Builds a minimal fetch-based API client bound to a base URL, exposing a request() helper that JSON-encodes bodies and content-negotiates JSON vs. text responses.

nodes.name: startApp
nodes.summary: Bootstraps the Web UI: resolves DOM anchors, builds the API client and view state, wires hash-based routing across all views (including the dashboard, via fetchDashboardData/renderDashboard), attaches nav/theme/filter/pagination event handlers, and opens an SSE connection for live updates.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines its view-rendering, event-wiring, and mutation-handler logic as nested closures (render, wireViewHandlers, handleMemoryEdit, etc.) that close over shared `state`, rather than top-level functions — the knowledge graph models only the enclosing startApp scope since these are private closures, not module-level declarations.

nodes.name: fetchDashboardData
nodes.summary: Fetches scheduler, hook-queue, Synapse-session, and metrics data from four endpoints in parallel via Promise.allSettled, unwrapping each into an independent {data, error} pair so one failing section doesn't block the others.

nodes.name: renderSchedulerSection
nodes.summary: Renders the scheduler status section as a jobs table (name, kind, enabled, next/last run, due, running) or a 'scheduler disabled'/'unavailable' message depending on data state.

nodes.name: renderHookQueueSection
nodes.summary: Renders the hook ingestion queue section showing pending count, max pending, and saturation state, or an 'unavailable' message on error.

nodes.name: renderSynapseSection
nodes.summary: Renders the active Synapse sessions table (session ID, agent, workspace, task context, expiry), or a 'No active sessions'/'unavailable' message depending on data state.

nodes.name: renderMetricsSection
nodes.summary: Renders the system metrics section showing process uptime, database size, and heap/RSS memory usage, or an 'unavailable' message on error.

nodes.name: renderDashboard
nodes.summary: Assembles the full observability dashboard by concatenating the scheduler, hook-queue, Synapse, and metrics sections into one HTML block, defaulting each to an 'unavailable' fixture when its data is missing.

nodes.name: cache-entry.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the CacheEntry model, covering constructor defaults, TTL expiration and remaining-TTL math, access tracking, promotion/eviction heuristics, value updates, and toJSON/fromJSON round-tripping.

nodes.name: cache-l1-memory.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for L1MemoryCache covering get/set/delete/clear/invalidatePattern/preWarm/getStats, LRU eviction under a size limit, adaptive TTL extension, expired-entry cleanup, and intelligent TTL derived from access patterns.
nodes.languageNotes: Injects L1 cache limits per test by mutating the shared singleton `config` through an unsafe cast to its private `set()` method, restoring production defaults in `afterEach`.

nodes.name: CacheEntry.ts
nodes.summary: Data model for a single entry in the hierarchical (L1/L2) cache, tracking TTL, access count/frequency, and size, with promotion/eviction heuristics and JSON serialization for persistence.
nodes.languageNotes: Generic class `CacheEntry<T>` implements the shared `ICacheEntry<T>` contract from `@massa-ai/shared`; `fromJSON`/`getDefaultTTL` are static factory helpers used to rehydrate entries and pick per-level defaults.

nodes.name: CacheEntry
nodes.summary: Generic cache entry tracking value, TTL, and access stats; exposes isExpired/getRemainingTTL/getAccessFrequency/shouldPromote/shouldEvict heuristics, an update() mutator, and toJSON/fromJSON round-trip plus a static per-level default-TTL lookup.

nodes.name: l1-memory-cache.ts
nodes.summary: Fastest tier of the hierarchical cache: a Map-backed in-memory LRU cache with size-limited eviction, periodic cleanup of expired entries, and adaptive/intelligent TTL calculated from recent access-interval patterns.
nodes.languageNotes: Layers a heuristic 'intelligent TTL' - derived from the average interval between the last 10 accesses - on top of standard LRU eviction (Map insertion order) and adaptive TTL extension on frequent reads, plus a background setInterval sweep started in the constructor.

nodes.name: L1MemoryCache
nodes.summary: In-memory LRU cache reading its size/TTL limits from shared config; get() promotes TTL on frequent access and re-orders entries for LRU, set() evicts the least-recently-used entry when over the size budget, and a background cleanup loop removes expired entries.

nodes.name: db-guard.ts
nodes.summary: Guards against a DEDICATED-stack process accidentally binding the shared production PostgreSQL database, plus URL validation and DB-name extraction helpers built on DATABASE_URL. Documents a real footgun where Bun auto-loads the repo-root .env and silently binds the shared massa_ai DB.
nodes.languageNotes: The exported assertDedicatedDbAllowed is a no-op unless MASSA_AI_DEDICATED=1, and is meant to be called immediately after env loading and before any DB client initialization — a fail-fast guard pattern rather than a runtime check embedded in the pool constructor.

nodes.name: int-env.ts
nodes.summary: Provides parsePositiveIntEnv for safely parsing positive-integer environment variables, avoiding the Number(env) || default bug where an explicit 0 is silently replaced by the default unless the caller opts in via { allowZero }.
nodes.languageNotes: The allowZero opt-in distinguishes 'unset/garbage, use default' from 'explicit zero is a valid value' — used for knobs like MASSA_AI_PROXY_TIMEOUT_MS where 0 means 'disable timeout' versus reaper intervals where 0 would cause a tight loop.

nodes.name: db-guard.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the DEDICATED-stack DB guard and integer env parsing utilities, covering URL validation, shared-vs-isolated DB name detection, the dedicated-mode fail-fast guard, and parsePositiveIntEnv's zero-handling behavior.

nodes.name: requirePostgresDatabaseUrl
nodes.summary: Validates and returns a usable PostgreSQL connection URL from DATABASE_URL (or an explicit argument), throwing before any DB pool is initialized if the URL is missing, malformed, uses a non-Postgres protocol, or lacks a database name.

nodes.name: getDbName
nodes.summary: Extracts and lowercases the database name (last path segment, query stripped) from a Postgres connection URL, returning null when the URL is unset or unparseable.

nodes.name: isSharedDb
nodes.summary: Checks whether a given database URL resolves to the shared/live massa_ai database name.

nodes.name: assertDedicatedDbAllowed
nodes.summary: Fail-fast guard that throws if a process flagged MASSA_AI_DEDICATED=1 would bind the shared production database instead of an isolated one; no-op when the flag is unset.

nodes.name: parsePositiveIntEnv
nodes.summary: Parses a positive integer environment variable, falling back to a default for unset, non-numeric, negative, or non-integer values; optionally honors an explicit 0 via { allowZero } instead of flooring it to the default.

nodes.name: config-cli.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the mcp-client `massa-ai-config` CLI, covering parseOptions flag parsing and every runCli command (init/path/show/set/use/recover) against a temp XDG_CONFIG_HOME.

nodes.name: captureConsole
nodes.summary: Test helper that temporarily swaps console.log/console.error to capture CLI output and exit code for assertions.

nodes.name: mcp-stdout-clean.test.ts
nodes.summary: Regression guard verifying the MCP stdio server emits nothing on stdout during startup (a pure JSON-RPC channel) while all logs route to stderr — protects the stdio handshake from the Bug 3 dotenv/logger leak.
nodes.languageNotes: Spawns the compiled server under a throwaway HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME so the first-run 'write default config' branch — where the original leak hid — actually executes; inheriting the developer's HOME would silently skip that path.

nodes.name: spawnMcp
nodes.summary: Spawns the built MCP server binary under an isolated temp HOME and collects its stdout/stderr/exit code as a promise.

nodes.name: recover-project.test.ts
nodes.summary: Behavior tests (T34/N42) for recoverProjectPath: a valid projectId re-associates the Workspace row and preserves the projectId alias-chain, while an unknown projectId returns found:false without calling update. Prisma is mocked via mock.module.

nodes.name: config-cli.ts
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for `massa-ai-config` (mcp-client variant) — manages the ~/.config/massa-ai/config.json file: init/show/set/use embedding provider (Ollama/Mistral/OpenAI), and delegates the `recover` command to recoverProjectPath.

nodes.name: help
nodes.summary: Prints the `massa-ai-config` usage banner listing every subcommand and example invocation.

nodes.name: parseOptions
nodes.summary: Parses `--flag value` / `--flag` style CLI arguments into an options record.

nodes.name: runCli
nodes.summary: Main command dispatcher: routes init/path/show/set/use/recover subcommands to config load/save operations and the dynamically-imported recoverProjectPath helper.

nodes.name: recover-project.ts
nodes.summary: Implements recoverProjectPath (N42) — re-associates an indexed project's Workspace row with a new filesystem path via a Prisma update, without re-indexing, preserving the projectId alias-chain (M16/M17).

nodes.name: recoverProjectPath
nodes.summary: Looks up a Workspace by projectId and, if found, updates its projectPath to newPath, returning the old and new paths; returns found:false when no matching project exists.

nodes.name: agents-install.test.ts
nodes.summary: Integration tests (T7) for the `massa-ai-config agents install/uninstall` subcommand — spawns the real CLI via spawnSync to verify it writes 15 ownership-tagged specialist .md files to the OpenCode agents directory, preserves user-authored agents on uninstall, and is idempotent on re-install.

nodes.name: runCli
nodes.summary: Test helper that runs the config-cli.ts source file via `bun run` with overridden HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME env vars and captures stdout/stderr/exit code.

nodes.name: config-cli.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the OpenCode plugin's `massa-ai-config` CLI, covering parseOptions parsing and runCli commands (init/path/show/set/use) against a temp XDG_CONFIG_HOME — the OpenCode-specific sibling of the mcp-client config-cli suite.

nodes.name: captureConsole
nodes.summary: Test helper that temporarily swaps console.log/console.error to capture CLI output and exit code for assertions.

nodes.name: config-cli.ts
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for the OpenCode plugin's `massa-ai-config` — manages embedding config like the mcp-client variant, plus an `agents install/uninstall` subcommand that copies the 15 bundled subagent specialist .md files into OpenCode's user or project agents directory with ownership tagging.

nodes.name: help
nodes.summary: Prints the `massa-ai-config` usage banner including the `agents install/uninstall` subcommand.

nodes.name: parseOptions
nodes.summary: Parses `--flag value` / `--flag` style CLI arguments into an options record.

nodes.name: runCli
nodes.summary: Main command dispatcher: routes init/path/show/set/use subcommands like the mcp-client CLI, plus an `agents` subcommand that copies or removes massa-ai-owned specialist .md files under OpenCode's agents directory.

nodes.name: project-reset.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the POST /api/v1/project/reset route's lexical/semantic clear lifecycle (vector, keyword, symbol, memory deletion) and its M8 audit-log attribution (op, actor, scope, meta), using mock.module to stub out core repositories.

nodes.name: reset
nodes.summary: Test helper that POSTs a reset request body to the mounted Elysia app and returns the parsed status/JSON response.

nodes.name: events.test.ts
nodes.summary: Coverage for the SSE `/api/v1/events` route — heartbeat frames, auto-close after max duration, and the cancel-hook teardown regression (the stream's start-return cleanup used to be dead code), using env-overridden short timer intervals.

nodes.name: drain
nodes.summary: Polls the SSE reader on a short interval, accumulating decoded chunks for a fixed window so heartbeat/close frames can be asserted on.

nodes.name: web-ui-errors.test.ts
nodes.summary: Edge-path coverage for the `/ui` and `/ui/*` static asset routes — mocks fs/promises to force disabled-flag, static-dir resolution failure, missing index.html, path traversal, asset read failure, and SPA-fallback branches.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Test helper issuing a GET request against the mounted Elysia app and returning status, raw text, parsed JSON (if any), and content-type.

nodes.name: app-renderers.test.ts
nodes.summary: Large rendering-logic suite for the static web UI — exercises the markdown fallback renderer, project/search/handoffs/checkpoints/memory-browser/proposals view renderers, theme toggling, and the write-mode gate against a hand-built fake DOM and fetch/EventSource harness.

nodes.name: makeFakeDom
nodes.summary: Builds a minimal fake `document`/element tree (createElement, getElementById, event handlers, child tracking) so app.js's DOM-manipulating renderers can run outside a real browser.

nodes.name: dashboard.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the dashboard data-fetch aggregator (fetchDashboardData) and its section renderers (scheduler, hook-queue, synapse, metrics) — covering fulfilled, rejected-Error, and non-Error rejection paths for each parallel API call.

nodes.name: index.test.ts
nodes.summary: Trivial smoke test asserting the web-ui package's WEB_UI_PACKAGE_MARKER constant equals "@massa-ai/web-ui", confirming the type-check-anchor entry point loads.

nodes.name: route-contract.test.ts
nodes.summary: Contract regression pinning the checkpoints-view renderer to a golden JSON fixture captured from the live `/api/v1/checkpoints/list` response, so renderer/route field-shape drift (e.g. `type` vs `checkpointType`) fails loudly instead of leaving the view silently empty.

nodes.name: write-mode.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the static app's markdown-to-HTML fallback renderer (marked+DOMPurify fallback), HTML escaping, and write-mode gating/proposal rendering behavior.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Type-check anchor entry point for the @massa-ai/web-ui package — exports a package marker constant only; the real browser bundle is the zero-build static asset set (index.html, styles.css, app.js) served verbatim by the Tools API at /ui/*.

nodes.name: index.html
nodes.summary: Single-page shell for the read-only massa-ai Memory Browser — hash-routed nav (projects/memory/search/handoffs/proposals/checkpoints/dashboard), a no-FOUC theme bootstrap script, and a module script tag loading the zero-build app.js bundle.
nodes.languageNotes: Loads marked and DOMPurify from a CDN for markdown rendering, and reads the persisted dark/light theme from localStorage before the stylesheet paints to avoid a flash of unstyled content.

nodes.name: styles.css
nodes.summary: Dependency-free stylesheet for the web UI memory browser — CSS custom properties for a light theme with a `[data-theme="dark"]` override, plus layout rules for the topbar, filters, data grids, cards, pager, and markdown content areas.
nodes.languageNotes: Theming is done entirely with CSS custom properties (--bg, --fg, --accent, etc.) redefined under a [data-theme="dark"] selector, so index.html's inline bootstrap script only needs to toggle one root attribute.

nodes.name: prisma.config.ts
nodes.summary: Prisma CLI configuration for packages/core — loads .env from the package root, points Prisma at prisma/schema.prisma and prisma/migrations, and forwards DATABASE_URL as the datasource URL when set.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses Prisma's newer declarative prisma.config.ts (defineConfig) rather than the legacy package.json "prisma" key.

nodes.name: compression-index.test.ts
nodes.summary: Smoke test for the compression service barrel (services/compression/index.ts) — verifies CodeCompressor is exported, constructable, and reports the CODE_STRUCTURE compression strategy.

nodes.name: context-controller.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for ContextController's budget allocation, working-set selection, and memory-section formatting logic — builds a fake controller sharing the real class's prototype methods to exercise orchestration behavior without triggering the heavy SearchController/MemoryController/KeywordSearch dependency chain.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately avoids importing or constructing the real ContextController; instead it builds a plain object exposing the same method surface so selectWorkingSet/formatMemorySection can be unit-tested without the heavy singleton chain.

nodes.name: buildFakeController
nodes.summary: Constructs a fake ContextController-shaped object with injectable searchProject/memorySearch/compressorHandle overrides, used to drive budget-allocation and working-set-selection assertions.

nodes.name: decorator-heavy.ts
nodes.summary: Polyglot e2e fixture exercising native tree-sitter structural extraction against heavy TypeScript decorator usage (class + method decorators) plus an intentionally-unresolvable import, used to validate the structural parser's resilience.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines stacked class decorators (@Injectable, @Component) with a method decorator and a deliberately-broken import ("./does-not-exist") to prove the structural extractor degrades gracefully instead of failing the whole file.

nodes.name: PolyRoot
nodes.summary: Decorator-annotated fixture class with a `title` field and a decorated `decoratedMethod`, used to test structural extraction of decorated class members.

nodes.name: polyFactory
nodes.summary: Factory function that constructs and returns a new PolyRoot instance.

nodes.name: usesGhost
nodes.summary: Calls the unresolved `ghost` import to verify the extractor tolerates references to a non-existent module.

nodes.name: indent-method.py
nodes.summary: Polyglot e2e fixture for Python structural extraction — a nested inner class plus mixed top-level function/method indentation, used to validate the tree-sitter Python grammar's handling of nested class and function scopes.
nodes.languageNotes: Nests an Inner class inside Outer to probe how the structural extractor handles indentation-delimited nested scopes rather than brace-delimited ones.

nodes.name: Outer
nodes.summary: Fixture class containing a nested Inner class and a top_level_method, used to test extraction of nested Python class scopes.

nodes.name: module_function
nodes.summary: Trivial module-level function (returns z - 1) used as a top-level extraction fixture.

nodes.name: use_outer
nodes.summary: Instantiates and returns an Outer instance, exercising a cross-scope constructor call for the fixture's call graph.

nodes.name: poly.dart
nodes.summary: Polyglot e2e fixture for Dart symbol extraction — a class with a constructor and method plus a top-level function, used to confirm Dart imports are deliberately left unparsed so the file lands in the symbol graph disconnected from PageRank import edges.
nodes.languageNotes: The file's own header comment documents that Dart imports are not parsed by the structural extractor, so this fixture is intentionally PageRank-disconnected (no incoming/outgoing import edges) even though its symbols are correctly extracted.

nodes.name: PolyDart
nodes.summary: Fixture class with a `name` field, a constructor, and a `greet()` method returning a templated string.

nodes.name: polyTopLevel
nodes.summary: Top-level Dart function that constructs a PolyDart and combines its greet() string length with the input n.

nodes.name: poly.go
nodes.summary: Go polyglot e2e fixture declaring a top-level exported function and an exported struct type, plus an unexported function that calls the first to exercise cross-symbol call-graph extraction.
nodes.languageNotes: Go's export convention is capitalization-based: PolyGo and PolyStruct are exported because they are capitalized, while the lowercase usePolyGo is package-private.

nodes.name: PolyGo
nodes.summary: Top-level Go function that adds 1 to its integer argument; exported and called by usePolyGo in the same fixture.

nodes.name: PolyStruct
nodes.summary: Simple exported Go struct with a single integer ID field, used as a minimal structural-key fixture.

nodes.name: poly.kt
nodes.summary: Kotlin polyglot e2e fixture declaring a class with a method and a companion object constant, alongside two top-level functions, exercising native Kotlin structural extraction.
nodes.languageNotes: The companion object demonstrates Kotlin's mechanism for static-like members attached to a class.

nodes.name: PolyKotlin
nodes.summary: Kotlin class with an integer id constructor property, a describe method returning a formatted string, and a companion object constant.

nodes.name: polyTopLevel
nodes.summary: Top-level Kotlin function returning the length of a string argument.

nodes.name: makePolyKotlin
nodes.summary: Top-level Kotlin factory function constructing a PolyKotlin instance.

nodes.name: poly.rs
nodes.summary: Rust polyglot e2e fixture declaring a public function and a public struct, plus a second public function that reads the struct's field and calls the first function.

nodes.name: poly_rust
nodes.summary: Public Rust function that adds 2 to its i32 argument.

nodes.name: use_poly_rust
nodes.summary: Public Rust function that reads a PolyRust struct's id field and adds the result of calling poly_rust, demonstrating field access plus a function call.

nodes.name: PolyRust
nodes.summary: Public Rust struct with a single public i32 id field.

nodes.name: sentinel.c
nodes.summary: C polyglot e2e fixture with a function and a caller function, exercising structural extraction for the C grammar.

nodes.name: poly_c
nodes.summary: C function that returns its integer argument unchanged.

nodes.name: use_poly_c
nodes.summary: C function that calls poly_c with a literal argument.

nodes.name: sentinel.clj
nodes.summary: Clojure polyglot e2e fixture declaring a namespace with a single-argument function and a def that invokes it, used to probe structural extraction for a language without native tree-sitter grammar support in this pipeline.
nodes.languageNotes: This file has no native tree-sitter grammar in the extraction pipeline, so its structure was recovered by direct source inspection rather than the bundled extractor.

nodes.name: poly_clojure
nodes.summary: Clojure defn in the poly.clojure namespace that returns its argument unchanged; public by default since it carries no ^:private metadata.

nodes.name: sentinel.cpp

layers.name: Tool Handlers Layer
layers.description: Thin MCP tool-handler modules in packages/core/src/tools/ (schema plus delegation, no business logic) -- the outermost entry surface of the product that both transports ultimately invoke; the import graph shows it calling down into controllers and services (34 and 6 edges respectively), so it behaves as an entry/handler layer rather than the generic 'utility' pattern its directory name would naively suggest.

layers.name: Controllers Layer
layers.description: Orchestration layer in packages/core/src/controllers/ that composes multiple services and owns side-effects, sitting between the thin tool handlers and the domain services they coordinate (18 import edges into services) -- an internal orchestration layer, not an HTTP API layer.

layers.name: Service Layer
layers.description: The dominant domain-logic layer in packages/core/src/services/ -- search, synapse, embeddings, graph, structural parsing, memory, jobs, etl, scheduler, symbol graph, project-identity, hooks, executor, checkpoint, cache, web, workspace, metrics, handoff, and events -- the largest and most internally-cohesive layer in the codebase (intra-group import density 0.42).

layers.name: Data Layer
layers.description: PostgreSQL/pgvector persistence in packages/core/src/data/ (repositories, vector store, FTS) plus the data-model types in src/models/, the package-root Prisma config, one-off DB-provisioning scripts (create-3072d-table.ts, create-progress-memory.ts), and the core package barrel (src/index.ts) that declares the four-layer architecture.

layers.name: Test Layer
layers.description: All 371 test files across every package: packages/core's flat, unmirrored src/__tests__/ tree (292 files, not organized by subject layer) plus co-located *.test.ts siblings in packages/shared/src/config/, apps/tools-api/src/routes/ and middleware/, apps/mcp-client/src/, and every package's own __tests__/ directory. Kept as one cross-cutting layer rather than split by subject, since core's dominant test tree is structurally flat and cannot be cheaply attributed back to tools/controllers/services/data.

layers.name: Shared Utility Layer
layers.description: packages/shared/src/ -- the cross-cutting logger, runtime config loader (~/.config/massa-ai/config.json), env handling, and shared TypeScript types consumed by core and every app transport.

layers.name: REST API Transport
layers.description: apps/tools-api/src/ -- the Elysia REST server on :3333 (route handlers, middleware, and startup/health bootstrap wiring) that is one of the two transports over the single tool contract, and mounts the separately-layered Web UI dashboard at /ui.

layers.name: MCP Stdio Transport
layers.description: apps/mcp-client/src/ -- the MCP stdio server exposing 52 tools via tool-def JSON Schemas (src/tool-defs/) and the dual api-client/embedded-api-client clients behind ToolProxyApiClient, the second of the two transports over the same contract.

layers.name: Auxiliary App Surfaces
layers.description: Two smaller install/runtime surfaces beyond the two primary transports: apps/web-ui's dashboard (static JS/CSS/HTML served at /ui) and apps/opencode-plugin's in-process OpenCode plugin handlers.

tour.title: The Core Package Contract
tour.description: massa-ai has no single entry point -- it is a monorepo with one product package (packages/core) and several transports layered on top of it. This file is the product's own statement of its architecture: it re-exports the four enforced layers (tools, controllers, services, data) as the package's single import surface for every consumer, whether that consumer is the REST API, the MCP stdio server, or a test. Read it first, because the rest of this tour is organized around the four directories it names, in the order a request actually flows through them: tools -> controllers -> services -> data.
tour.languageLesson: TypeScript barrel files use `export * from './module'` to re-export an entire directory as one public surface. Because a re-export is not a value import, some static-analysis tools do not trace through it the same way as a normal `import` statement -- worth remembering when a file that is clearly 'central' shows no direct dependency edges.

tour.title: Tool Handlers Layer
tour.description: Following the contract from Step 1, `tools/` is the outermost layer that both transports ultimately call into: 31 files, one per MCP tool, each deliberately thin -- parse input, delegate, serialize output, no business logic. `search_project.ts` is a representative example: its entire job is to call `SearchController.searchProject` and serialize the result. This thin-handler discipline is what lets two very different transports expose the same tool contract without duplicating logic, since the real logic lives one layer down, in controllers.
tour.languageLesson: A 'thin handler' -- validate input, delegate, serialize output, no branching logic -- keeps an entry-point layer stable even as the transports calling it (HTTP, stdio, embedded) evolve independently underneath it.

tour.title: Controllers: Orchestration Layer
tour.description: One layer down from the tool handlers sit the six controllers -- Memory, Search, Context, Executor, Graph -- that own orchestration and side effects. `search-controller.ts` shows what that means concretely: before it runs a search it performs a two-tier admission preflight, optionally triggers an auto-reindex, applies glob include/exclude filtering, boosts results by Symbol-Graph centrality, and optionally reranks with an LLM judge. This is the layer where several services get composed into one coherent operation -- the tool handler from Step 2 only had to know to call `searchProject` once.

tour.title: The Search Facade Pattern
tour.description: The search controller's work continues into `ContextualSearchRLM`, the busiest file in the service layer by fan-out (26 outgoing dependencies) and one of the most depended-upon (22 incoming). Rather than let one class grow without bound, its methods were mechanically extracted into four `rlm-*.ts` companion files -- indexing, search execution, Synapse integration, and admin/stats -- each holding plain functions that take the RLM instance as an explicit first parameter. The structural analysis flags these five files as one of the codebase's most tightly coupled clusters, and together they run the hybrid vector-plus-Postgres-full-text search with reciprocal-rank fusion that the project is built around.
tour.languageLesson: Extracting a large class's methods into standalone functions that take the instance as their first argument (`doThing(rlm, args)` instead of `rlm.doThing(args)`) preserves the original public API while letting each concern live in its own file -- a pragmatic middle ground between one giant class and a full redesign.

tour.title: The ETL Indexing Pipeline
tour.description: Before any search or symbol lookup can work, a project has to be indexed -- that is this five-file pipeline. `pipeline.ts` orchestrates four sequential stages: `discover` walks the filesystem and hashes files to skip unchanged ones, ordering the rest by Symbol-Graph centrality; `parse` runs native tree-sitter grammars to extract symbols and imports; `resolve` turns raw import specifiers into concrete file paths and FQNs, handling monorepo path aliases; and `load` persists everything to the vector store, keyword index, and symbol database in per-batch transactions with deadlock retry. `pipeline.ts` itself has the third-highest fan-out of any file in the codebase, reflecting how much it coordinates.
tour.languageLesson: discover -> parse -> resolve -> load is the classic ETL shape (Extract, Transform, Load) applied to source code instead of business data; each stage is independently testable, and a pipeline like this can retry a single stage without redoing the others.

tour.title: Symbol Graph & Blue-Green Generations
tour.description: The `load` stage from Step 5 writes into the symbol graph, whose consumer-facing facade is `symbol-graph.service.ts` -- it answers go-to-definition, find-references, and dependency queries, and assembles the project map. What makes this subsystem distinctive is `graph-generation-coordinator.ts`: instead of mutating the graph in place, each ETL run builds a new versioned 'generation,' activated only once complete and lease-locked against concurrent writers -- a blue-green deployment pattern applied to a database table rather than a server fleet. `symbol-repository-factory.ts` is the Data-layer repository this all reads and writes through, reached via the `get*()`/`reset*()` factory convention used throughout the codebase; `workspace-manager.ts` ties a generation back to the workspace it belongs to.
tour.languageLesson: Blue-green deployment usually means routing traffic between two live server environments for a zero-downtime release; here the same idea is applied to data -- build a whole new 'generation' of the symbol graph in the background, then atomically flip a pointer to it, so readers never see a half-indexed graph.

tour.title: The PostgreSQL Data Layer
tour.description: Every repository you have seen so far -- memory, symbol, observations -- ultimately goes through two shared files: `db-connection.ts`, a lazily-created `pg` connection pool, and `prisma-client.ts`, the Prisma ORM singleton wired to that pool. `prisma-client.ts` is the single most widely depended-upon file in the entire codebase (36 incoming dependency edges), which tracks with massa-ai running on PostgreSQL 17 plus pgvector exclusively -- there is no SQLite fallback. Rounding out this step, `event-bus.ts` is the second-most depended-upon file (29 edges), a strongly-typed EventEmitter that decouples writers like the ETL pipeline from listeners such as hooks, jobs, and the SSE layer, and which reappears in Step 9.

tour.title: Synapse: Cross-Session Memory
tour.description: Synapse is the subsystem that gives the assistant memory across sessions -- roughly 28 service files handling scoring, inhibition, plasticity, metacognition, and prefetch, of which this is the load-bearing core. `session-store-pg.ts`, built directly on the Postgres foundation from Step 7, persists session state to `synapse_sessions`/`synapse_access_history` while serving synchronous reads from an in-memory mirror; `working-memory-buffer.ts` layers a session-scoped hot cache on top, matching new queries against past ones via Jaccard token overlap. These five files form one of the graph's most tightly coupled clusters, anchored by `types.ts`, the shared vocabulary -- query classification, metacognition flags, session shape -- the rest of the subsystem builds on.

tour.title: Graceful Degradation for LLM Features
tour.description: A recurring discipline across massa-ai is that every LLM-driven feature defaults OFF and falls back to a rule-based path; a single flag, `RLM_LLM_ENABLED=true`, is what turns them all on. `llm-client.ts` is the shared client every one of those features calls through -- it wraps an OpenAI-compatible Ollama endpoint with its own timeout enforcement and default-off gating built in. `bootstrap-service.ts` (seeds a freshly-indexed project's initial memories via LLM summarization, with a rule-based fallback) and `handoff-service.ts` plus `handoff-auto-injector.ts` (lets one session leave a note for the next, optionally LLM-polished, surfaced through the event bus from Step 7) are three concrete instances of the same pattern applied to three different features.
tour.languageLesson: A feature flag that a system degrades gracefully around -- rather than one that just hides a UI element -- has to be designed in from the start: every LLM call site here has a deterministic non-LLM fallback path, not merely an early return when the flag is off.

tour.title: Shared Utilities Across Packages
tour.description: `packages/shared` is the one piece of the codebase that both `packages/core` and every transport app depend on directly, for logging, environment/config loading, and shared TypeScript types. `env.ts` resolves and loads the nearest `.env` file, walking up directories to support the monorepo layout, seeds `process.env` from `~/.config/massa-ai/config.json` as a lower-precedence fallback, and handles a one-time legacy data-directory migration. This file runs at process startup for every one of the entry points still ahead in this tour, which is why it belongs here, at the seam between the core package and its consumers.

tour.title: REST API Transport
tour.description: `apps/tools-api/src/index.ts` is one of massa-ai's two transports -- a thin wrapper around the core package from Steps 1-9 -- and it has the single highest fan-out of any entry point in the codebase, directly wiring 18 route modules, 3 middleware modules, and startup validation before binding port 3333. The dependency-chain traversal rooted here reaches 25 files in one hop, more than from any other entry point; `routes/search.ts`, `middleware/auth.ts`, and `routes/web-ui.ts` are three representative examples, exposing the hybrid search from Step 4 over HTTP, validating the `x-api-key` header while exempting `/health` and `/swagger`, and mounting the static dashboard at `/ui`. This route-per-file, middleware-first wiring is what makes it possible to add a new tool without touching how authentication or error handling works.

tour.title: MCP Transport & the Two-Client Contract
tour.description: The second transport, and the primary way most users actually consume massa-ai, is the MCP stdio server. `index.ts` wires MCP SDK handlers for `tools/list` and `tools/call`, proxying each call through `call-tool-proxy.ts`, which translates an MCP CallTool request into an HTTP-shaped call by substituting path parameters into the tool's endpoint template. What makes this genuinely interesting is that there are two interchangeable implementations behind that same `ToolProxyApiClient` interface -- `api-client.ts` (real HTTP to the tools-api server from Step 11) and `embedded-api-client.ts` (dispatches directly to core services in-process when `MASSA_AI_EMBEDDED=true`) -- and keeping their endpoint maps identical is a tested contract, not just a convention.
tour.languageLesson: This is the Adapter pattern doing double duty: both api-client.ts and embedded-api-client.ts satisfy the same interface, so call-tool-proxy.ts never needs to know or care whether a tool call crosses a network socket or is just a function call in the same process.

tour.title: Declaring Tools as JSON Schema
tour.description: Every tool exposed through Step 12's MCP server needs a JSON Schema describing its name, inputs, and description -- that is what this cluster provides. `tool-definitions.ts` is a facade that concatenates per-domain `tool-defs/tool-defs-*.ts` modules -- search, memory, synapse, project, hooks-exec -- into one `TOOL_DEFINITIONS` array in a fixed, test-pinned order, plus a `getToolDefinition` lookup helper. Splitting one flat list into domain modules is what keeps this navigable at 52 tools and counting, and it closes the loop back to Step 2's tool handlers, since every schema here names the handler it describes.
